title: Public vs Private Apps | Aircall Developer Platform
snippet:
A Private App is built for a single Aircall account. It's the fastest way to get started — no review process, no marketplace listing, and no OAuth flow required. The app is authenticated using API keys scoped to your specific Aircall account.

###
Key characteristics
| | |
|---|---|
| Authentication | API key |
| Audience | Single Aircall account |
| Developer account | ❌ Not available |
| App listing | ❌ Not available |
| Tech partner program | ❌ Not required |
| Review process | None |
| Setup time | Minutes |

Public App
A Public App is built to be distributed to multiple Aircall customers. To build one, you must first join the [Aircall Technology Partner Program](https://aircall.io/partners/technology/)
Public Apps are intended to be published and discoverable by Aircall's customer base. Public Apps use OAuth 2.0 so each customer can securely connect their own Aircall account to your integration.
###
Best suited for
- SaaS companies building a native integration with Aircall
- Technology partners wanting to reach Aircall's customer base
- Integrations you plan to distribute, monetize, or showcase publicly
###
Key characteristics
| | |
|---|---|
| Authentication | OAuth 2.0 |
| Audience | Multiple Aircall customers |
| Tech partner program | Required |
| Developer account | ✅ Available |
| App listing | ✅ App Marketplace + Aircall product * |
| Review process | Required |
| Setup time | Days to weeks |
☝️ **The specifics of where and when your app gets listed depend on your journey through the partner program.*

title: Aircall API Review 2026: Features, Limits & Alternatives
snippet:
**Aircall's** [Public API](https://developer.aircall.io/api-references/) is a REST surface served from https://api.aircall.io/v1, with a growing v2 layer for select resources. It supports both [Basic Auth and OAuth 2.0](https://developer.aircall.io/api-references#authentication), covers calls, contacts, users, teams, numbers, messaging, webhooks, conversation intelligence, and AI Voice Agent endpoints, and ships with one official SDK (a front-end CTI library).

- You need API pricing transparency before committing. Aircall does not publicly state which plan tiers include API access or whether API calls are metered.

| **Pricing / access** | Bundled with paid Aircall plans (Essentials at $30/user/month); specific API access tiers not publicly documented |

Getting API access starts with a paid Aircall account. You generate API credentials from the Aircall Dashboard under Company Settings, where you create an api_id and api_token. The token appears only once at creation and cannot be recovered.

**OAuth 2.0** is required for technology partners building apps that serve multiple Aircall customers through the [App Marketplace](https://aircall.io/call-center-software-integrations/). The flow is an [authorization code grant](https://developer.aircall.io/tutorials/how-aircall-oauth-flow-works): Aircall redirects the installing admin to https://dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and scope=public_api.
The authorization code expires after 10 minutes and is exchanged for a permanent access_token. An optional state parameter prevents CSRF.
One thing to know: there is no self-serve OAuth registration. Partners must get client_id and client_secret by contacting Aircall at marketplace@aircall.io and applying through the [partner programme](https://aircall.io/partners/technology/). This gates marketplace app development behind manual approval.

Based on the developer documentation, API key generation is available from the Company Settings page, suggesting API access is bundled with a paid Aircall subscription rather than charged separately. The Essentials plan at [$30/user/month](https://aircall.io/pricing/) (annual, 3-user minimum) lists "100+ integrations and API access" as a feature, indicating API access on all tiers.

title: Overview
snippet:
> ###
> Messaging API access is not available for all subscription plans.
>
>
>
> All numbers must meet carrier registration requirements and local regulations before you can send messages.

Access to the Messaging API depends on how it's being used.
**Direct API access requires the Professional plan.**
If you are calling the Messaging API directly — for example, building your own integration or testing from your own account — your Aircall account must be on Professional. Contact your Customer Success Manager to upgrade.
**Access through an integration is available on any plan.**
If an integration is calling the Messaging API on your behalf, the Professional plan restriction does not apply — the integration can send and receive messages regardless of the plan your account is on.
> Message volume from both the API and the Aircall app is combined on your invoice. Per-message fees are identical regardless of the sending method.
##
Rate limits
Requests are limited per API token, over a 60-second window. The default is 120 requests per minute per token, and higher limits are set per token. A request over the limit returns `429` with `X-AircallApi-Limit`, `X-AircallApi-Remaining` and `X-AircallApi-Reset` headers.
